text.author: Lord Harris
text.title: Letter from Lord Harris on 11 February 1879
text.summary1: (human1) In a letter, a cricket player recounts a disturbance that broke out during a cricket match with the NSW Eleven when the opposing team objected to the decisions of the umpire, Coulthard, resulting in a mob rushing the play grounds and players.
text.summary2: (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929; postedited) A touring English cricket player recounts to a person called E. how their February match in Sydney descended into chaos when the NSW team objected to umpire Coulthard after a controversial run-out decision, prompting three mob invasions of the field, assaults on players, and eventually halting play amid accusations of betting-fueled misconduct.
text.summary3: (gpt4o) On February 11, in Sydney, a letter detailed how a cricket team's match against the NSW Eleven turned chaotic when alleged biased umpiring led to a disturbance fueled by betting men, resulting in aggressive behavior from the crowd and ending with no resolution to the umpire disagreement.
text.summary4: (Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct; postedited) A cricket match between a traveling team and the NSW Eleven was marred by a violent mob, sparked by the NSW Eleven's objection to umpire Coulthard, who was eventually cleared of any wrongdoing.
text.summary5: (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; postedited) The writer describes a cricket match in the Colonies where his team, faced disturbances from a mob and professional bettors who objected to the use of a professional umpire, leading to a heated and chaotic situation on the field.
